text:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran a focused sweep on prefill vs decode perf across FP16/FP8/INT8/4bit for long-context workloads (16k tokens). Observations below, tagging @alex @rachel for kernel selection thoughts.

alex: Nice, summary pls — what stands out? :eyes:

maya: TL;DR: quant modes improve end-to-end TPS but change TTFT profile: prefill gets much faster on lower-bit kernels except when calibration runs inline. Decode latency per-token often slightly worse for FP8/INT8 vs FP16 (kernel tradeoff), which hurts TTFT for short tail generations. Also saw KV-cache eviction stalls on microbatch boundaries for very long contexts.

rachel: Can you paste the numbers? even roughs.

maya: Sure — microbenchmark (single A100, seq_len=16k prefill + 512 decode, batch size=1, microbatching off):
```
Mode   | Prefill TTFT (ms) | Decode TTFT (ms) | Avg TPS (tokens/s)
FP16   | 1250              | 38               | 210
INT8   | 880               | 46               | 235
FP8    | 740               | 52               | 228
4bit   | 620               | 68               | 255

Note: TPS measured over full end-to-end (prefill+decode).
```

sam: Interesting that 4bit has best TPS but worse per-token decode. Looks like batching helps offset decode cost.

maya: Exactly. But one regression: when we enable the new per-layer calibration during first prefill (the dynamic scale estimator), prefill spikes to ~1.6x for INT8/FP8 because we run extra fused ops per layer. So overall TPS goes down unless calibration is moved offline.

toni: Which kernel path is being chosen for decode vs prefill? Is kernel selector swapping at runtime?

maya: Kernel selector picks decode-optimized kernels for smaller seqs by heuristic (seq_cutoff=1024) but for long prefill it picks prefill kernels. Problem is when microbatching + kv eviction triggers, we sometimes route a prefilling request through the decode path (fallback) which causes extra copies and KV reshuffle. That's the stall we saw.

perf-bot: Profiling summary attached: prefill kernels spend 42% time in matmul, 18% in kv_copy, 12% in scale/quant ops (if calibration enabled). Decode kernels show 55% matmul, 25% softmax, 8% kv_lookup.

alex: Two quick actionable items: 1) don't run calibration inline on first prefill — add a flag to run calibration as background job or during model load. 2) tighten kernel selector to prefer prefill kernels when input has kv_cache present.

rachel: Agreed. Also add metrics to detect "kv-reshuffle" events per request; we can alert if >0.1% of requests hit it.

maya: Proposed config snippet to force prefill route when kv present and disable inline calib:
```yaml
runtime.kernel_policy:
  prefer_on_kv: prefill
  seq_cutoff: 2048
runtime.calibration:
  mode: offline
  path: /var/lib/llm_calib
```

sam: Want to run an A/B with that config on a dedicated machine pool. I can spin one up and run the same 100-sample bench.

maya: Yep — can you also include longer tail tests (1k short requests mixed with occasional 16k prefill) to capture TTFT impact? The mixed workload is where decode per-token hurts perceived latency.

toni: One more thought: kernel packing for 4bit uses different kernel that favors throughput but increases decode loop overhead. We could add a lightweight decode-only microkernel for last 32 tokens to close the per-token gap. @alex can you estimate dev effort?

alex: Roughly 2-3 days to prototype microkernel, 1 week to bake and test across devices. Worth it if we see >5% p95 improvement for interactive use.

rachel: I'll open a tracking issue and link perf results + PR pointer to the commit that introduced inline calibration (0f3a9c). Also adding a dashboard tile for kv-reshuffle + calibration_time.

maya: Thanks — summary action items:
- disable inline calibration by default (move to offline)
- tighten selector to prefer prefill when KV present
- add kv-reshuffle metric and alert
- bench new microkernel for decode tail
- run mixed workload A/B on dedicated pool

sam: I'll provision pool and run tests, will post results here. :rocket:

perf-bot: Test run queued: run_id=1854123-AB1, expected duration ~22m.

maya: Great, keeping this thread for follow-ups. If anyone finds other regressions in perf capture please paste snippets. Especially watch for extra device-host memcpy during fallback path.
